locus_a: main article, Introduction: "we have assembled and evaluated a library of over 500 peptoid candidates for mRNA delivery, over 200 of which are highlighted in this work"
locus_b: main article, Results: "a large and diverse library of 221 peptoid molecules". SI Table S1 lists peptoids numbered 1-221; SI Table S9 adds 222-266. Tracker states 200.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. No row depends on the library size. 03_enumerated.csv contains the 45 peptoids of Table S9 and says so.
why: The three numbers are not in conflict once read carefully: >500 is everything ever synthesised, 221 is the clustered screening library, 266 is the highest peptoid index in the SI, and "over 200 highlighted" is what the tracker's 200 is rounding. We enumerate 45 and emit 5, so the reconciliation is reported rather than resolved.

locus_a: main article Figure 1B, lipid panel, prints "C12H23" beside the Dod squiggle. Dodecyl is C12H25.
locus_b: SI page 20 (Figure S7) legend prints "Dod (C12)" and draws the chain explicitly; curation/lib chains measures 12 stroked segments -> 13 merged vertices -> 12 carbons.
why: The Figure 1B formula is one hydrogen short. If it were read as a degree of unsaturation, Table S4's "Branched/Unsaturated Monomers" column would count Dod -- it prints 0 for peptoid 226 (Apd-Dod-Dod-Dod-Dod). Three independent routes give saturated C12 and only the printed H-count disagrees, so the H-count is the typo.

locus_a: main article Figure 1B prints "C18H31" beside Ode. Octadecyl is C18H37; C18H31 is the formula of a linoleyl (18:2) chain.
locus_b: No other locus defines Ode. It appears only in SI Table S1's screening library.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. Ode is not used by any peptoid in 222-266 and is listed in 01_blocks.csv as not enumerated.
why: Unresolvable from what we hold, and it costs nothing: no emitted row uses Ode. Recorded so that a later curation of the 221-member library does not assume octadecyl.

locus_a: main article Figure 1B, cationic panel, labels a pyrrolidin-3-ylmethyl structure "Mpp".
locus_b: the SAME panel labels a 4-methylpiperazin-1-ylpropyl structure "Mpp".
what_we_emitted: Nothing. Neither structure is used by peptoids 222-266; 01_blocks.csv lists Mpp as not enumerated.
why: One three-letter code, two drawn structures, in one figure. Any sequence in SI Table S1 containing Mpp is therefore ambiguous. This is the single largest reason the 221-member library is not enumerated here.

claim: Monomer codes absent from the drawn pool
locus_a: SI Table S9 sequences use the codes "Eae" (peptoid 228) and "Dme" (peptoid 231).
locus_b: main article Figure 1B's monomer pool draws neither code.
what_we_emitted: Eae: enumerated as 2-(ethylamino)ethanol, which is in the SI Materials list and whose composition the printed calculated exact mass confirms exactly (1046.94). Dme: NOT ENUMERATED -- peptoid 231 is excluded from 03_enumerated.csv.
why: Eae has a Materials-list reagent and a mass that agrees to 0.00 Da. Dme has neither a drawing nor a unique reading: its composition is pinned at C4H10N by the printed mass, but C4H10N is also Figure 1B's drawn "Mae" (methylaminopropyl), so mass cannot choose. Guessing it would invent a connectivity.

locus_a: main article Table 1 column header reads only "luciferase expression (p/s)" and names no organ.
locus_b: the sentence citing it reads "(Table 1 and Figure 5D)", and Figure 5D is captioned "Total Fluc bioluminescence in balb/c liver". Elsewhere in the paper "Total Flux" means whole-animal (e.g. SI Figure S7B).
what_we_emitted: Both readings, in two columns: organ_as_printed = "not stated in Table 1" and organ_inferred = "liver". Every row's curation_note repeats it.
why: The two differ by the extrahepatic fraction, which the paper puts below 3% for Nutshell 236 at 7.5 mg/kg but does not measure at 0.125 mg/kg for the other four. Small, not zero, and not ours to pick.

claim: Stated optimum for total lipid carbons
locus_a: main article Results and Conclusions: "maximal predicted expression was achieved using peptoids containing 5-6 total lipid monomers, 55 total lipid carbons" and "the optimal performance coming from 6 lipid monomers and 55 carbons".
locus_b: main article Table 1, "model predicted" row: total lipid carbons 52.5 +/- 8.8.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. No emitted field depends on the model's optimum.
why: 55 is not 52.5, and the discrepancy changes a claim in the same paragraph: the text says peptoid 245's 44 carbons are "just outside of the predicted range", but 52.5 - 8.8 = 43.7, so 44 is INSIDE Table 1's own stated interval. The text's "55" and Table 1's "52.5 +/- 8.8" cannot both be the model's output.

locus_a: SI Table S9, peptoid 253 (Apd-Dod-Ehx-Dod-Ehx): Calculated 936.80, Found 1107.91 -- a difference of +171.11 Da where every clean row differs by +1.01.
locus_b: SI Table S9, peptoids 245 and 255: Found Exact Mass 1107.91, byte-identical.
what_we_emitted: The structure from the CALCULATED column only. 253 is enumerated and its calculated mass agrees with our structure to 0.00 Da.
why: 253's Found cell is a copy of another row's. Detected by the derived [M+H]+ regularity (35/45 rows at +1.01 +/- 0.02 Da), which the paper never states -- see 07_qc.json found_minus_calculated_is_a_proton. No structure depends on the Found column.

locus_a: SI Table S9, peptoid 262: Calculated 1387.22, Found "2.00".
locus_b: every other row's Found value is a mass near the calculated one.
what_we_emitted: The structure from the CALCULATED column only.
why: "2.00" is not a mass. Same detector, same conclusion: the Found column is unreliable on 10 of 45 rows (228 +54.07, 231 +2.14, 232 +19.05, 241 +2.01, 242 +2.01, 248 -299.20, 249 +2.03, 250 +2.37, 253 +171.11, 262 -1385.22) and nothing we emit uses it.

locus_b: a percentage of encapsulated mRNA cannot be negative.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. No particle-property column is emitted; the corpus in-vivo definition excludes diameter and zeta and this curation emits no encapsulation value.
why: Recorded because it is evidence about Table S5's general reliability for anyone who later wants its pKa or hemolysis columns.

claim: Peptoid 236 measured twice at the same nominal dose
locus_a: main article Table 1: 1.08 +/- 0.41 x 10^9 p/s at 0.125 mg/kg, 6 h, n = 3.
locus_b: SI Figure S7B: a separate total-flux panel for 236 vs 266 at "2.5 ug IV dose", 6 h, n = 3. For a 20 g mouse 2.5 ug is 0.125 mg/kg -- the same nominal dose.
what_we_emitted: Only the Table 1 value. SI Figure S7B is recorded in 00_value_sources.json as a value source deliberately not digitised.
why: The paper never states a relationship between the two runs and never pools them. We do not digitise Figure S7B, so we make no claim about how far apart they are -- only that the same peptoid at the same nominal dose appears in two independent experiments, which is why they could not share one Experiment_ID.
